<thought>Carbon is evident from the noticeable M+1 peak (~13 % of the base peak). The unusually high M+2 intensity (~33 % of the base) cannot be explained by carbon alone and matches the combined contribution of a chlorine atom (≈24 % M+2) plus one or more sulfurs (≈4 % per S). The M+3 peak (~4 %) further supports the presence of sulfur (34S) together with 13C. No 1:1 M+2 pattern for bromine or the smaller contributions of nitrogen, oxygen, or hydrogen are discernible. Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon, chlorine, and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl', 'S']</final_answer>
